page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-2 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the E2 instance family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon core with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include any bundled local storage or GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results position this instance in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scores 1105.98, falling into the bottom 25% of tested hardware, while the multi-core score of 1452.89 sits in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show 80.99 GB/sec for small cached blocks, dropping to 13.03 GB/sec for large uncached read operations and 11.11 GB/sec for large write operations. In application-specific benchmarks, the instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 906.0 and a multi-core score of 1073.0. Redis SET operations reach 1.34 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is measured at 1.39 GB/sec.

The e2-highcpu-2 represents a low-cost entry point for compute-focused workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation but have minimal memory requirements. The primary tradeoff is the highly constrained memory capacity of 2.0 GB, which limits its utility for memory-intensive applications or large-scale databases. It is suited for lightweight, CPU-bound tasks such as basic text processing, minor compilation tasks, small-scale web serving, or running small language models, where it achieves 164.01 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M parameter model.
